1000573.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Latin Cerēs (“Ceres, the Roman goddess of grain and agriculture”), from Proto-Italic *Kerēs (“with grain; Ceres”). De Vaan reconstructs the latter from a Proto-Indo-European s-stem *ḱerh₁/₃-os (“nourishment, grain”), ultimately from *ḱerh₁/₃- (“to feed”).
The name has traditionally also been compared with Latin creō (“to create, beget”) and crēscō (“to grow”), a comparison still given in some Norwegian reference works. De Vaan, however, regards crēscō as belonging to a different Proto-Indo-European root.

1004925.etyen:
From fyrste (“prince”) + familie (“family”), literally “prince's family”.
The first element fyrste (“prince”) is from Middle Low German vurste (“prince; literally, first”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *furistaz (“first, foremost”), from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂- (“before”). The second element familie (“family”) is borrowed through German Familie from Latin familia (“household, family”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place”).
Compare Danish fyrstefamilie and German Fürstenfamilie (“princely family”).
